Follow and drive your **Fronius Wattpilot** EV charger (Wattpilot Home and
Go, 11 and 22 kW; Wattpilot Flex in test) from Gladys, **on your local
network**: Gladys talks to the charger's WebSocket, as the Fronius
Solar.wattpilot app does at home. No cloud, no Fronius account.

> **Developed without the hardware: feedback welcome.** This integration was
> written from the protocol as documented and implemented by other open-source
> projects (the `wattpilot` library of joscha82, the Home Assistant integration
> of mk-maddin), and tested against a fake charger, without a Wattpilot at hand.
> If something looks wrong, open an issue on the GitHub repository with the
> integration logs.

This integration is not affiliated with Fronius International GmbH.

## Requirements

- A Fronius Wattpilot (Home or Go, 11 or 22 kW) connected to your Wi-Fi.
  The Wattpilot Flex is supported in theory (its password check differs) but
  untested.
- The **password of the charger**: the one you chose in the Solar.wattpilot
  app when you set the charger up (the app asks for it to connect).
- A **fixed IP address** for the charger, set in your router (DHCP
  reservation): the integration reaches it by its address.
- Gladys and the charger on the same network (port 80 of the charger
  reachable from Gladys).
- Gladys 5.2.0 or later.

## Configuration

1. Install the integration from **Integrations → Install from GitHub** (or the
   store), then open its **Configuration** tab.
2. **Charger IP address**: for example `192.0.2.10`.
3. **Charger password**: the password of the Solar.wattpilot app. It stays in
   Gladys (a secret field) and is never sent anywhere but to the charger, as a
   hash.
4. **Refresh interval**: how often the measures (power, current, energy) go
   to Gladys, 15 seconds by default.
5. **Language of the feature names**: names given to the features of new
   devices and language of the error texts (French by default).
6. Save: the charger appears in the **Discovery** tab. Add it.
7. The **Test the connection** button says whether the charger is connected
   (name, serial number, firmware) or why not.

## Refresh and network use

The integration keeps **one WebSocket connection** open to the charger, which
pushes its changes by itself: nothing is polled. The charger sends its
measures several times a second while charging; the integration forwards them
to Gladys at the refresh interval, and **at once** when something you act on
changes (car state, mode, current, override, error). Only the values that
changed are sent, plus every value again every 6 hours so a stable one never
shows "no recent value". Gladys also polls the device as a fallback; the
integration then skips a publication it has just made.

When the connection drops, the integration reconnects after 5 s, 10 s, 30 s,
then every minute. A refused password is retried every 10 minutes only. A
charger silent for a minute is pinged, and the connection is opened again if
it does not answer.

## The charger device

| Feature            | What it shows                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Connector          | Available (no car), Occupied (car plugged in), Unavailable (offline), Faulted (error)                         |
| Charging state     | Charging, Vehicle connected (waiting), Paused (vehicle): charge complete, Paused (charger): not allowed, Idle |
| Car plugged in     | 1 when a car is plugged in                                                                                    |
| Charging power     | Total power, W                                                                                                |
| Power L1, L2, L3   | Power per phase, W                                                                                            |
| Current L1, L2, L3 | Current per phase, A                                                                                          |
| Session energy     | Energy since the car was plugged in, kWh                                                                      |
| Total energy       | The charger's meter, kWh: Gladys' energy monitoring computes the consumption and its cost from it             |
| Charging current   | **Command**: the current offered to the car, from 6 A to 16 A (11 kW) or 32 A (22 kW)                         |
| Charging mode      | **Command**: Default, Eco, Next Trip — the modes of the Solar.wattpilot app                                   |
| Charge override    | **Command**: Follow the mode, Forced charge, Forced stop                                                      |
| Temperature        | The hottest sensor of the charger, °C                                                                         |
| Error              | The Wattpilot error in words ("None" when all is well)                                                        |
| Online             | 1 while the charger is connected                                                                              |

The **charging mode** only switches between the modes; their settings (solar
surplus and price limit of Eco, departure time and energy of Next Trip) stay
in the Solar.wattpilot app and Solar.web: this integration does not duplicate
solar charging. **Forced charge** charges whatever the mode decides; **Follow
the mode** gives the decision back to it.

The current cannot go above the limit set in the app ("maximum current"): the
integration refuses it with a message rather than sending it.

## Widget

Add the **Fronius Wattpilot** widget to a dashboard and pick the charger. It
shows the live power, the session energy and the charging current, the state
(Ready, Charging, Waiting, Charge complete, Error), the mode, an override in
force and the error if any. Four buttons: **Charge** (forced charge), **Stop**
(forced stop), **Auto** (follow the mode) and **Settings…**, which opens a
form to set the current and the charging mode. The override in force carries a
check icon.

## Scene trigger

**Wattpilot charge finished**: the car stopped drawing after a charge (it is
full, or reached the limit set in the car or the app). Optionally pick the
charger. The following actions can use `energy_kwh` (energy of the session)
and `charger` (its name). It fires once per charge, never at startup.

"Car plugged in" needs no trigger: use the **Car plugged in** feature (changes
to 1) in a "device value" trigger.

## Scene actions

- **Set the Wattpilot charging mode**: Default, Eco or Next Trip.
- **Force or stop the Wattpilot charge**: forced charge, forced stop, or
  follow the mode.

The charging current needs no action of its own: it is a feature, set with
Gladys' usual "control a device" action.

## Scene examples

- **Solar during the day, full at night**: at 08:00, "Set the Wattpilot
  charging mode" to Eco; at 22:00, to Default.
- **Tell me when the car is full**: trigger "Wattpilot charge finished", then
  send a message "Charge finished: \{\{triggerEvent.data.energy_kwh\}\} kWh".
- **Protect the main breaker**: when the house power goes over a threshold,
  set the charging current to 6 A; when it goes down, back to 16 A.
- **Leaving early tomorrow**: from a button on the dashboard, "Force or stop
  the Wattpilot charge" to Forced charge; at 07:00, back to Follow the mode.

## Troubleshooting

- **"No answer"**: check the address, that the charger is on the Wi-Fi, and
  that Gladys and the charger are on the same network.
- **"Something answers, but not a Wattpilot"**: the address is another device
  (the router, the inverter...).
- **"The charger refused the password"**: enter the password of the
  Solar.wattpilot app again (mind the case). After a refusal, the integration
  only retries every 10 minutes: press **Test the connection** to retry now.
- **"Connected, but the charger did not send its status in time"**: restart
  the charger, then press **Test the connection**.
- **A command fails with "the charger refused the request"**: the value is
  outside what the charger accepts right now.
- The integration logs say the rest: set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` for the detail of
  every change.

## Limits

- One charger per Gladys. Two Wattpilots: open an issue.
- The feature names and the maximum current are fixed when the device is added
  (a Gladys rule): to change the language, delete the device and add it again.
- No access to the RFID cards, the schedules, the solar and price settings, the
  phase switching or the cable lock: they stay in the Solar.wattpilot app. The
  cable lock is deliberately not exposed.
- Gladys keeps a connection open to the charger, next to the app and maybe
  another home automation box. How many the charger accepts at once is not
  documented: if the app cannot connect while Gladys is, say so in an issue.
- Wattpilot Flex: its password check (bcrypt) follows the Home Assistant
  integration, untested on a real Flex.
- Tested against a fake charger and published protocol descriptions only (see
  the note at the top).

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Fronius Wattpilot asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before you start | `section` | No | Gladys talks to the Wattpilot directly on your local network, like the Fronius Solar.wattpilot app does at home. Give the charger a fixed IP address in your router, then enter it below with the password of the charger: the one you chose in the app when you installed it. |
| Charger IP address | `string` | No |  |
| Charger password | `secret` | No | The password set in the Solar.wattpilot app. It stays in Gladys and never leaves your network. |
| Refresh interval | `select` | No | How often the measures go to Gladys. A change of state, mode or current is sent at once. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Names given to the features of new devices, and language of the error texts. |

## How to install Fronius Wattpilot in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Fronius Wattpilot appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-wattpilot:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-wattpilot](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-wattpilot).

Fronius Wattpilot requires Gladys `>=5.2.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.
